title: Simultaneous regular-pair approximation over a complete Cohen trait

source.place: Agent-formulated algebraic input for the complete-base version of Expose XVI section 3.7, first paragraph, printed p.254. ILO I Theorem 2.9 (Cohen), printed p.9, I Theorem 10.3(i) (Popescu), printed p.17, and IV Theorem 4.1.8, printed pp.56--57, provide the presentation and approximation ingredients; the exact simultaneous regular-pair formulation here is not asserted verbatim by ILO.

proof.text: Choose a Cohen ring $C$ with $C/pC\simeq k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-rings-exist], and lift this residue isomorphism to $C\to R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-ring-lift-complete-local]. The regular local ring $R$ is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. This map is local: an element outside $pC$ has nonzero residue in $k$ and hence is a unit in $R$. It is injective: every nonzero element of the DVR $C$ is a unit times $p^n$, and $p^n\ne0$ in the characteristic-zero domain $R$. Completeness makes $C$ henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian], and $k$ is separably closed, so $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait. Since $\ell$ is invertible in the local ring $R$, $\ell\ne p$; its residue in $C/pC$ is nonzero, so $\ell$ is invertible in $C$.

Put $P=C[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_d)$. The power-series structure theorem [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] makes $P$ complete regular local of dimension $d+1$. The continuous map $\pi:P\to R$, $X_a\mapsto t_a$, exists by summing power series in the complete ring $R$. It is surjective by the following explicit expansion. For $r\in R$, lift its residue to $c_0\in C$. If a polynomial approximation has error in $\mathfrak m^N$, write that error modulo $\mathfrak m^{N+1}$ as a finite sum of degree-$N$ monomials in the $t_a$ with coefficients in $k$, and lift these coefficients to $C$. Adding the corresponding degree-$N$ polynomial improves the error to $\mathfrak m^{N+1}$. The successive homogeneous polynomials define a series in $P$ mapping to $r$. The map is local, with the prescribed residue identification and prescribed ordered parameters.

source.place: Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary); Tag 032A, final proof paragraph, with the prescribed generators t_a. The expansion is written out here.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters], $\ker\pi$ is generated by an initial part of a parameter system of $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], quotienting by $c$ such parameters has dimension $d+1-c$. Since $P/\ker\pi\simeq R$ has dimension $d$, $c=1$; write $\ker\pi=(h)$ with $h\notin\mathfrak n^2$. Express $p=\sum_a t_a r_a$ in $R$, lift $r_a$ to $b_a\in P$, and set $f=p-\sum_aX_ab_a$. Then $f\in\ker\pi$ and its image in $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$ has coefficient $1$ on the basis vector $p$. In particular $f\notin\mathfrak n^2$. Writing $f=uh$ forces $u$ to be a unit, since otherwise $uh\in\mathfrak n^2$. Thus $R=P/(f)$, compatibly with $t_a=X_a\bmod f$, and $f\bmod(X_1,\ldots,X_d)=p$.

Let $A=C[X_1,\ldots,X_d]$ and $J=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_d)$. Its $J$-adic completion is $P$: at level $N$, both $A/J^N$ and $P/(JP)^N$ consist uniquely of the finitely many monomials $X^E$ with $|E|<N$, their coefficients taken modulo $p^{N-|E|}$. The criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] gives this description on $P$; on polynomials it is the expansion of the generators of $J^N$. Hence the compatible finite quotient maps are isomorphisms. Taking their inverse limits and using the completeness of $P$ from [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] identifies $\widehat A_J$ with $P$, as $A$-algebras. This argument also checks that the map is the canonical completion map, not an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 032C; finite-level coefficient argument for the (p,X)-adic polynomial completion.

proof.text: The complete Noetherian local ring $C$ is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence]. Thus $A$ is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], and is a G-ring by the definition [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular] to $A,J$ and the canonical identification of Step 4: $A\to P$ is regular. Both rings are Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-smoothing], $P$ is a small filtered colimit of smooth $A$-algebras. Popescu gives smooth morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$; by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] each $A\to B$ is a smooth ring map, so it is finitely presented by [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal], reindex this diagram by a small nonempty directed set $I_0$, writing $P=\operatorname{colim}_iB_i$. The same lemma preserves the colimit cocone, so the maps to $P$ remain $A$-algebra maps.

source.place: more-algebra.tex Tags 07QW (proposition-ubiquity-excellent), 07QU (lemma-finite-type-over-excellent), 07QT (definition-excellent), 0AH2 (lemma-map-G-ring-to-completion-regular); smoothing.tex Tag 07GC (theorem-popescu); categories.tex Tag 0032 (lemma-directed-category-system). Smooth affine morphism versus smooth ring map: node lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine.

proof.text: By finite-data descent [lemma-nagata-filtered-colimit-finite-data], all $b_a$ lift to one $B_{i_0}$. Restrict to $i\ge i_0$ and let $b_{i,a}$ be their compatible images. Define $f_i=p-\sum_aX_ab_{i,a}$ and $E_i=B_i/(f_i)$. The $E_i$ form a compatible system with colimit $P/(f)=R$. Indeed a compatible family of ring maps out of the $E_i$ is exactly a compatible family out of the $B_i$ killing all $f_i$, equivalently a map out of $P$ killing $f$. Also $E_i/(X_1,\ldots,X_d)=B_i/(p,X_1,\ldots,X_d)$. This is a smooth $k$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], hence regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-fibre-regular-local]. The structural map $E_i\to R\to k$ is surjective because it contains the surjection $C\to k$; denote its maximal kernel by $q_i$.

We check the local sequence at $q_i$, without assuming regularity has descended. Let $Q_i\subset B_i$ be the inverse image of $q_i$ and $T=(B_i)_{Q_i}$. Smoothness makes $B_i$ flat over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. The sequence $X_1,\ldots,X_d,p$ is regular on $A$: successive quotients by the variables are polynomial rings over the domain $C$, and the final quotient by $p$ is $k$. Tensoring the injective multiplication maps of this sequence with the flat module $B_i$, using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], preserves their injectivity. Localization at $Q_i$ preserves each injection: if $x(y/s)=0$, some $v$ outside $Q_i$ satisfies $vxy=0$ in the relevant quotient, hence $vy=0$ by injectivity there, and $y/s=0$. Every resulting quotient in $T$ is nonzero because all these elements lie in $Q_i$. Since $f_i=p$ modulo the variables, $X_1,\ldots,X_d,f_i$ is a regular sequence in $T$. The Noetherian local permutation lemma [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-permutation-noetherian-local] makes $f_i,X_1,\ldots,X_d$ regular. Consequently the ordered variables are a regular sequence in $(E_i)_{q_i}=T/(f_i)$. Here $T$ is Noetherian: $B_i$ is finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: Tags 00TA (lemma-smooth-syntomic), 00HD (lemma-flat), 00LJ (lemma-permute-xi); the displayed injection and quotient argument proves the needed specialization.

proof.text: The quotient of $(E_i)_{q_i}$ by the variables is a localization of the regular ring of Step 6, so is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring]. Together with Step 7, [lem-exc-regular-local-lift-regular-sequence-quotient] makes $(E_i)_{q_i}$ regular local. The ring $E_i$ is finite type over $C$, hence excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Its regular locus is open by the J-2 clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring], applied to $E_i$ as a finite type algebra over itself. Choose a principal open containing $q_i$ inside that locus. By [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood], shrink once more around $q_i$ so that the prescribed ordered variables form a regular sequence on the whole affine ring. Every inverted element has nonzero image in $k$, hence maps to a unit in $R$; therefore $E_i\to R$ extends across each shrink.

The resulting regular affine Noetherian scheme has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Its local rings are domains by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]; hence different irreducible components cannot meet, since a local domain has a unique minimal prime. Remove all components except the one through $q_i$, and choose a principal open still containing $q_i$ in this complement. Its ring $F_i$ is a domain. To see reducedness explicitly, a nilpotent element becomes zero in each local domain; if it were nonzero its proper annihilator would lie in a maximal ideal and its localization there would be nonzero. Thus the ring is reduced, and having just one minimal prime makes it a domain. This shrink preserves the regular sequence: all multiplication injections remain injective under localization by [lem-pc-localization-preserves-nonzerodivisor], and the final quotient is nonzero because $q_i$ remains. The composite of the successive principal shrinks is itself a principal shrink of $E_i$.

source.place: properties.tex Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components); algebra.tex Tag 00NP (lemma-regular-domain). The finite-component and reducedness argument is written out.

proof.text: Use all good principal shrinks, not independently chosen unrelated models. An index is $(i,g)$, $i\ge i_0$, where $g\in E_i\setminus q_i$ and $(E_i)_g$ is integral regular with the ordered variables a regular sequence. Step 9 supplies such an index over every $i$. Put $(i,g)\preceq(j,h)$ if $i\le j$ and the image of $g$ is a unit in $(E_j)_h$; the transition is the unique map induced by $E_i\to E_j$. Any two indices have an upper bound: first choose $j$ above both stages, then take a good principal shrink at $j$ and also invert the images of both denominators. These images avoid $q_j$, so the shrink remains nonempty and good. This is a small directed preorder; apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to its thin filtered category to obtain a directed set $I$. The colimit is still $R$: every element of $R$ lifts to some $E_i$ and hence to a good shrink; a fraction mapping to zero has numerator zero in $R$, thus that numerator vanishes at a later $E_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero] and then in a common good upper shrink. Denominators map to units in $R$, so all maps to $R$ exist.

source.place: categories.tex Tag 0032 (lemma-directed-category-system); finite-data construction of the directed localization system. No additional approximation lemma is invoked.

proof.text: For an index of the final directed set write $F_i$ for its ring. It is a finite type $C$-algebra, as $B_j$ is finite presentation over $A=C[X_1,\ldots,X_d]$ and the construction uses one quotient and one principal localization. The map $C\to F_i\to R$ is injective on $C$. Since $F_i$ is a domain, this makes it torsion free over the PID $C$, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat]. Thus $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}F_i$ is integral regular affine, flat and finite type over $S$. Set $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}(F_i/(X_1,\ldots,X_d))$. Its ring is a principal localization of $B_j/(p,X_1,\ldots,X_d)$, so it is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring] and Step 6, and it is an $\mathbf F_p$-algebra. The closed immersion is cut out by the displayed regular sequence of length $d$. All transition maps preserve the variables because the original diagram is over $A$; therefore these closed immersions and their equations are compatible.

source.place: more-algebra.tex Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), PID case; algebra.tex localization of regular rings and Tag 00T4.

proof.text: By Step 10, $\operatorname{colim}_iF_i=R$. Quotienting the compatible variables gives $\operatorname{colim}_iF_i/(X_1,\ldots,X_d)=R/(t_1,\ldots,t_d)=k$: a map from the left-hand colimit is exactly a compatible family of maps from $F_i$ killing the variables, equivalently a map from $R$ killing the $t_a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition-core] and [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition-affine-comparison], taking spectra identifies the limits of the two affine systems with $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$, compatibly with the closed immersion and with the functions $t_a$. All transitions between affine schemes are affine. Finally choose finitely many algebra generators of each $F_i$ over $C$; the resulting surjection from a polynomial algebra gives a closed immersion $V_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_S\subset\mathbf P^n_S$, verifying quasi-projectivity as claimed.
